label: Calculations
description: Numerical problems: Hardy-Weinberg, breeder's equation, Hamilton's rule, selection coefficients, life-history.

cards.term: 100 individuals: 36 AA, 48 Aa, 16 aa. Compute p, q, and check HWE.
cards.definition: p = (2·36 + 48)/200 = 120/200 = 0.6. q = 0.4. Expected: p²=0.36, 2pq=0.48, q²=0.16. Observed = expected → in HWE.

cards.term: Disease frequency 1/2,500. Compute carrier frequency.
Disease frequency 1/10,000 (autosomal recessive). Compute q and carrier frequency.
cards.definition: q² = 0.0001 → q = 0.01. p ≈ 0.99. Carrier freq = 2pq ≈ 0.0198 ≈ 1/51. Carriers ~100× more common than affected.

cards.term: p=0.7 in HWE. Compute genotype frequencies.
X-linked recessive at q=0.08. Compare male vs female prevalence.
cards.definition: Males (hemizygous) affected at q = 0.08 = 8%. Females affected at q² = 0.0064 = 0.64%. Ratio ≈ 12.5×; males far more affected.

cards.term: Mean trait 170 cm; breeders' mean 178 cm; h² = 0.5. Predict R and next-gen mean.
cards.definition: S = 178 − 170 = 8 cm. R = h²·S = 0.5·8 = 4 cm. Next-generation mean ≈ 174 cm.

cards.term: Mean milk yield 25 L/day; breeders 30 L/day; h² = 0.3. Predict R.
cards.definition: S = 5. R = 0.3·5 = 1.5 L/day. Next-generation mean ≈ 26.5 L/day.

cards.term: h² = 0 (purely environmental trait). Predict R for any S.
cards.definition: R = h²·S = 0·S = 0. No response to selection regardless of how strongly you select. The trait does not evolve.

cards.term: Variance partition: V_A=60, V_D=10, V_E=30. Compute h² and H².
cards.definition: V_P = 100. h² = V_A/V_P = 0.60. H² = (V_A+V_D)/V_P = 70/100 = 0.70. Selection responds to h² = 0.60.

cards.term: Hamilton's rule: cost C=1, sibling r=0.5. Required B?
cards.definition: rB > C → 0.5·B > 1 → B > 2. Saving a sibling must yield >2 offspring units of benefit.

cards.term: Hamilton's rule: cost C=1, half-sib r=0.25. Required B?
Hamilton's rule: cost C=1, first cousin r=0.125. Required B?
Hawk-Dove ESS for V=10, C=20.
cards.definition: p_Hawk* = V/C = 0.5. Mixed ESS at 50% Hawks. Mean fitness = ½·V·(1−p) = 0.5·10·0.5 = 2.5 (also = mean Hawk payoff at ESS).

cards.term: Selection-vs-drift threshold for Ne = 100 diploids.
cards.definition: Threshold |s| ≈ 1/(2Ne) = 1/200 = 0.005. Alleles with |s| > 0.005 are under selection; |s| < 0.005 effectively neutral (drift dominates).

cards.term: Wahlund: subpop A (p=0.9, N=50), subpop B (p=0.1, N=50). Pooled p̄, expected vs observed het.
cards.definition: p̄ = 0.5. Naive HWE expects 2pq = 0.50 het. Observed pooled het = (2·0.9·0.1·50 + 2·0.1·0.9·50)/100 = 0.18. Deficit = 0.32. Wahlund effect.

cards.term: Population doubles every generation. After 5 generations from 10 individuals, population size?
Sickle-cell allele equilibrium with s_AA-AA = 0.1 (malaria cost on AA), s_SS-SS = 1.0 (lethal aa). Compute q*.
cards.definition: q* = s_AA-AA / (s_AA-AA + s_SS-SS) = 0.1 / (0.1 + 1.0) = 0.091. ~9% HbS allele frequency at equilibrium.

cards.term: Allele frequency change under selection: p(t+1) = p·w_A / w̄. Given p=0.5, w_A=1.1, w_a=1.0, compute Δp.
Effective population size for 50 males and 200 females (sex-ratio formula).
cards.definition: Ne = 4·N_m·N_f / (N_m + N_f) = 4·50·200/250 = 40,000/250 = 160. Despite census N=250, drift acts on Ne=160.

cards.term: Inbreeding for full-sib mating one generation: F.
cards.definition: F (full-sib mating) = 1/4. Expected genotype freqs at biallelic locus: p² + Fpq, 2pq(1−F), q² + Fpq.

cards.term: Generation time 5 yr; 10 mutations per generation; 10,000 yr elapsed. Number of mutations accumulated.
cards.definition: Generations = 10000/5 = 2000. Mutations = 2000·10 = 20,000.

cards.term: Carbon-14 half-life 5,730 yr. Sample retains 12.5% of original ¹⁴C. Age?
MacArthur-Wilson: small island, distance to source halved. Predict S* change qualitatively.
cards.definition: Distance halved → immigration curve raised → S* increases (curves intersect at higher S). Larger area lowers extinction → S* also rises.
